items.text: High. A two-year full-time MBA at a brand-name institute can cost several lakh rupees before you earn a single BA rupee, plus the opportunity cost of two years out of the workforce.

items.heading: Most "Is Business Analyst
items.text: Most "is business analyst a good career" articles start with salary. That is backwards. The salary chart later in is close to meaningless if the daily work itself does not suit you, because business analysis has one central, non-negotiable skill demand that other "communication-friendly" careers do not: comfort sitting inside genuine disagreement long enough to resolve it.

items.heading: This Is the Decision Most
items.text: This is the decision most "how to become a business analyst" content treats as obvious, get an MBA if you can afford it, without actually running the numbers. It deserves a real comparison, not a brand-name assumption.

rows: Fastest for campus-hire consulting and large-enterprise BA programmes, placement cells route MBA graduates directly into structured BA or associate-consultant tracks.
Slower on average, because there is no campus pipeline doing the sourcing for you, but IT services and banking hire "any graduate" year-round once you have a proof-of-work artifact.
Higher on day one, especially at consulting firms and large enterprises that run dedicated MBA-entry BA or associate-consultant bands.
Lower on day one, but the gap narrows fast once you have 2-3 years of real requirement-ownership and domain depth behind you.
What actually closes the gap later
The MBA brand opens the door faster; it does not automatically make you better at extracting a clear requirement from a confused stakeholder, that is still a built skill, not a taught one.
Domain depth, a track record of projects that shipped on scope, and (later) CBAP close most of the pay gap by the 4-6 year mark, without the MBA fee or the two lost years.
